facts.statement: Stensioella heintzi is known only from fossils found in the Lower Devonian Hunsrück slate of Germany.
facts.quote: It is only known from the Lower Devonian Hunsrück slate of Germany.

facts.statement: It is tentatively classified as one of the most basal placoderms based on shoulder joint similarities.
facts.quote: Stensioella is tentatively placed within Placodermi as being among the most basal of all placoderms

facts.statement: Paleontologist Philippe Janvier suggests that Stensioella was a holocephalid rather than a placoderm.
facts.quote: The paleontologist, Philippe Janvier suggests that it was actually a holocephalid, and not a placoderm at all.

facts.statement: It is often considered a relative of the order Pseudopetalichthyida and a basal placoderm.
facts.quote: Se le suele considerar un pariente del orden Pseudopetalichthyida y se le considera un placodermo basal.

facts.statement: The species is characterized by the presence of teeth in the jaw and branchial spines on the gill arches.
facts.quote: se caracteriza por la presencia de dientes en la mandíbula y branquioespinas en los arcos branquiales.

facts.statement: Stensioella lived during the Emsian stage, between 410.62 and 399.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Emsian to Emsian (410.62 to 399.5 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The animal had an elongated body, a whip-like tail, and long, wing-like pectoral fins.
rejected.quote: Stensioella heintzi has an elongated body, a whip-like tail, and long, wing-like pectoral fins.

rejected.statement: Its armor consisted of a complex mosaic of small, scale-like tubercles rather than large bony plates.
